items.name: Carrot Fennel Chutney
steps: Measure 24 g (about 2 tablespoons) of citrus and keep it separate from the vegetables until their surfaces are dry.
Steam the grated carrot briefly and let it lose its surface heat. Maintain a steady steam for 2–4 minutes and check until the vegetables are hot through and bend without tasting raw.
Blend it with cilantro, crushed fennel, oil, and lemon. Blend for 30–40 seconds, stop to scrape the sides, and leave the texture described rather than aerating it.
Season the textured chutney and serve it at room temperature. Wait 2 minutes at room temperature, taste a small spoonful, and correct the salt or acidity without thinning the mixture.
Rest Carrot Fennel Chutney for 30 minutes, taste only after the flavors settle, and refrigerate any unused portion in a clean covered container.
items.guidance: Carrot Fennel Chutney is a concentrated accompaniment; use a small portion with a compatible meal Vata: pair it with warm moist food and avoid an oversized raw portion. Pitta: reduce sourness and hot chili where present. Kapha: keep oil and sweetener restrained while favoring pungent aromatics.

items.name: Beet Cumin Chutney
steps: Measure 22 g (about 1 tablespoon) of citrus and keep it separate from the vegetables until their surfaces are dry.
Cool the cooked beet until warm rather than hot. Spread the cooked component on a plate for 8–10 minutes, turning it once, until it is at room temperature before blending.
Pulse it with mint, cumin, oil, and lemon to a coarse relish. Work in 6 short pulses, pausing between them so the mixture stays cool and retains the intended texture.
Add salt and rest the ruby chutney for five minutes. Stir the salt through for 20 seconds, then stand at room temperature for 5 minutes before the final taste.
Rest Beet Cumin Chutney for 25 minutes, taste only after the flavors settle, and refrigerate any unused portion in a clean covered container.

steps: Measure 18 g (about 1 tablespoon) of citrus and keep it separate from the vegetables until their surfaces are dry.
Mash the steamed pumpkin while it remains warm. Keep this stage to 5–7 minutes over gentle medium heat and stop when a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Beat in ginger, cumin, oil, and lemon until glossy. Whisk for 60 seconds, scraping the bottom and corners until no dry pockets or lumps remain.
Season the chutney and leave a few soft pieces visible. Wait 2 minutes at room temperature, taste a small spoonful, and correct the salt or acidity without thinning the mixture.

steps: Measure 360 g (about 24 tablespoons) of citrus and keep it separate from the vegetables until their surfaces are dry.

Reduce the chopped tomatoes in sesame oil until their raw aroma fades. Maintain low heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a spoon drawn across the base leaves a trail that closes slowly.

Stir in ground sesame and crushed cumin and cook until thick. Maintain gentle medium heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a spoon drawn across the base leaves a trail that closes slowly.
Season the chutney and cool it to warm before serving. Spread the cooked component on a plate for 8–10 minutes, turning it once, until it is at room temperature before blending.
Rest Tomato Sesame Chutney for 30 minutes, taste only after the flavors settle, and refrigerate any unused portion in a clean covered container.

steps: Weigh 420 g yogurt into a dry bowl and let it stand for 10 minutes; whisk for 30 seconds so the base is smooth before the cooked or drained additions enter.
Squeeze the grated cucumber lightly and loosen the yogurt. Squeeze for 20–30 seconds in a clean cloth until the vegetable no longer drips, then loosen it with a fork.
Fold in the vegetable, mint, and crushed fennel without beating. Fold for 30 seconds with the heat off, stopping as soon as the yogurt is evenly streaked so the base stays thick.
Season the raita and take off its chill before serving. Wait 2 minutes at room temperature, taste a small spoonful, and correct the salt or acidity without thinning the mixture.

Dry the blanched bean pieces until no steam remains. Leave the salted or cooked pieces in one layer for 5 minutes, then blot every cut face so no visible moisture remains.
Coat them with fennel, lemon, sesame oil, and salt. Turn for 30 seconds with the heat off, stopping when every surface is glossy but no dressing pools at the bottom.
Rest the crisp pickle for thirty minutes before using. Cover loosely and stand at room temperature for 30 minutes, then taste one piece and keep the remainder crisp and intact.
Transfer Green Bean Fennel Quick Pickle to the dry jar after its stated rest, close the lid, and refrigerate any unused portion with a clean spoon kept nearby.

items.name: Cumin Coriander Table Masala
steps: Set a completely dry heavy skillet, grinder, and jar beside the stove for Cumin Coriander Table Masala; wipe away all moisture and warm the skillet over medium-low heat for 2 minutes.

Toast each seed separately until aromatic and let all of them cool. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone. Spread them on a plate for 8 minutes before grinding or combining.
Combine the spices and grind them to a medium-fine powder. Work with the heat off for 1 minute, lifting from the bottom until the color and texture are even throughout.
Transfer the masala to a dry jar and use it by the pinch. Transfer immediately to the dry jar, close it away from steam, and label it before returning it to a cool cupboard.
Keep Cumin Coriander Table Masala in a cool, dry cupboard; use a clean, dry spoon and close the labeled jar immediately after each serving.
